question: Pranav Cements Ltd, a fictional listed company, plans to buy coal for five years from a trading firm owned by its promoter's son, at prices slightly above the market. The promoter says the firm is reliable and the deal should be approved quickly at the next board meeting. As an independent director, discuss the governance and compliance issues you would raise.
sources: Companies Act, 2013 - Section 177 (audit committee) and Section 188 (related party transactions)
SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 - Regulation 23

points.label: It is a related party transaction
points.description: A close family member of a person who controls the company, and an entity he controls, are related parties under Ind AS 24; the son's firm is also likely to be a related party under the Companies Act and SEBI definitions, so the coal contract is a related party transaction.
points.basis: Companies Act, 2013, Section 2(76) definition of related party; Ind AS 24 definition of related party

points.label: Audit committee and board approval
points.description: The transaction needs prior approval of the audit committee, where only independent directors vote on related party transactions, and board approval with the interested directors not taking part.
points.basis: Companies Act, 2013, Sections 177 and 188; SEBI LODR Regulation 23

points.label: Arm's length and ordinary course
points.description: Prices above market suggest the deal is not at arm's length; the committee should ask for independent price quotes, the business reason and alternatives before deciding.
points.basis: Companies Act, 2013, Section 188 (exemption only for ordinary-course arm's length transactions)

points.label: Shareholder approval if material
points.description: If the contract crosses the materiality threshold for listed companies, shareholders' approval is needed and related parties cannot vote in favour.
points.basis: SEBI LODR Regulation 23, material related party transactions

points.label: Disclosure and director duty
points.description: The transaction must be disclosed (to stock exchanges and in the financial statements under Ind AS 24); an independent director should record dissent if concerns are not resolved.
points.basis: Ind AS 24 disclosures; Companies Act, 2013, Section 149 and Schedule IV (duties of independent directors)
